standard_prerequisites.name: Consistency, tableau sense
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set Gamma is inconsistent when there are B_1,...,B_n in Gamma and a closed tableau for {True B_1,...,True B_n}; consistent otherwise.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the notion whose contrapositive the proof runs (2528-2532).

standard_prerequisites.name: Tableau soundness
standard_prerequisites.statement: The unit's soundness theorem: a closed tableau for a finite set of signed formulas is not satisfiable.
standard_prerequisites.use: It derives unsatisfiability of the finite subset (2532-2536).

core_obligations: Contrapositive: suppose Gamma is inconsistent, so finitely many B_i in Gamma have a closed tableau for {True B_1,...,True B_n} (2528-2532).
By tableau soundness no structure satisfies all the B_i, so Gamma is not satisfiable (2532-2536).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack inconsistency to a finite closed tableau.

difficulty_reason: The counted corollary is the author corollary at source lines 2523-2526: if Gamma is satisfiable then it is consistent. The author proof (2528-2537) is a complete contrapositive: inconsistency yields a finite B_1,...,B_n in Gamma and a closed tableau for {True B_1,...,True B_n}; the unit's tableau soundness theorem (cited by label) gives no structure satisfying all the B_i; hence Gamma is unsatisfiable. Nothing is omitted.
